note: A second declaration of the same task. Since 22 Nov 2026 the map page's default export (site/data/map_paths_with_drafts_palm_mount.json) and the talk pictures are both made from this file; data/map_task_cones.json is the first declaration, with the finger aimed at the ball. Made from that file by changing three things. The finger stands on the palm beside the ball ("mount": "palm") instead of being aimed at it; this is not the placement demos/backwards_lookup.py was run with for outputs/backwards_lookup.json. Backwards lookups on this placement are in outputs/backwards_lookup_with_drafts_palm_mount.json (demos/backwards_lookup.py --mount palm --drafts --tag palm_mount), which leaves out both fingers of two pneu-nets, and in outputs/backwards_lookup_with_drafts_palm_mount_lines_22nov.json, which ranks them too, one row for each line logged in their records (one input swept, the other held). Neither shows the second check here: the lookup ranks a share of travel along the needed direction, not the return, and these two runs rank only lines logged in a record, so the stroke line this file's second check picks, worked out on the surface with the far chamber held at its top level, is not among them. A third run, outputs/backwards_lookup_with_drafts_palm_mount_worked_out_lines_22nov_b.json (the same command with --worked-out-lines), does rank that stroke line, on rows marked as worked out, not simulated; it is still a share of travel along the needed direction, not the return check. The second check lets the stroke start from any held tip position ("return_clear.stroke_from"). And no push is declared, because the needed push is only worked out for the aimed placement. The task, finger count, yaw, half-angle and stroke are unchanged. Read by tools/export_map_paths.py. Each entry declares one task drawn on the map as a cone on the three tip-travel axes. "task" names a file in data/tasks. "n", "mount" and "yaw_deg" are the placement of the finger on the object that the needed direction is worked out for; they are the ones demos/backwards_lookup.py was run with for outputs/backwards_lookup.json. "half_angle_deg" is how far from the needed direction a tip position may lie and still count as inside; "half_angle_basis" says where that number comes from. "least_travel_m" is the least tip travel along the needed direction, or null where the task file states none, with "least_travel_note" saying so. "stroke" (optional) gives the cone a far end: "angle_deg" is the wave's commanded stroke, "source" pins where it is read from (a Wave_manip commit, file, sha256, key and command-line flag) and "basis" says what it means; the exporter turns it into the tip travel for one stroke, from the task file's ball radius and contact-ring altitude. Nothing here comes from, or goes into, data/records. "push_basis" and "push_threshold_ratio" (given together, or neither) ask for the push each finger must make to hold the task's object: the basis says how it is worked out and what it means, and the threshold ratio is the share of the needed push a record must reach to count as meeting it. "return_clear" (optional, only with a stroke) asks for a second check: after the stroke the finger must break contact and come back to its start clear of the object. "basis" says how that is read from the tip positions; "drawn_depth_m" is how much further out of the object than its stroke path the tip must be able to sit, all along the stroke, and how deep the page draws the band for it; "drawn_depth_basis" says where that number comes from.

cones.half_angle_basis: A choice made for the display, not a limit measured on the task. Inside 45 degrees the tip has moved further along the needed direction than across it (the squared cosine is above one half). The task file gives no angle. The range of angles for which the records inside the cone are exactly the stored turners is worked out by tests/test_export_map_paths.py and is not used to choose this number.
cones.least_travel_note: The task file states no least tip travel, so the cone has no floor: any travel inside the angle counts. Its far end is one stroke of the wave.

stroke.basis: The stroke angle is the wave's commanded sweep of each fingertip about the turn axis during contact, read from the same run command the task file takes its duty from. That run only settled the ball, so this is the commanded stroke, not a measured turn of the ball. The tip travel for one stroke is the stroke angle times the contact ring's distance from the turn axis (ball radius times the cosine of the ring altitude, both from the task file), the inverse of the repository's own turn-per-stroke rule (gramian_workshop.arrange.Arrangement.turn_per_stroke_deg). Here the stroke may start from any tip position the finger holds, not only from rest: see return_clear.stroke_from_basis. The tip's real target is an arc about the turn axis; the straight cone with a far end is a simplification.

return_clear.basis: After each stroke the finger must let go of the ball and come back to where the stroke began without dragging the ball back with it. So the return path must sit further out of the ball than the stroke path, at every travel along the stroke: less travel along the contact normal, which points into the ball. This is read from free tip positions only; nothing here simulates the ball, or the push on it. Distance from the ball's curved surface is not used, because the stroke is drawn straight and a straight path leaves a ball by geometry alone. A finger with one input has one tip position at each travel, so it can only come back the way it went.
return_clear.drawn_depth_basis: A choice made for the display, not a clearance measured on the task. The task file states none. tests/test_export_map_paths.py checks that, on the records held under this declaration, every pass or fail is the same for any depth from a hundredth of a millimetre up to 7 mm.
return_clear.stroke_from_basis: On this placement the finger stands beside the ball, and a second input can carry its tip towards the ball or away from it. So the stroke need not start at rest: the finger may first bring its tip onto the ball with one input, then stroke with the other. The stroke path is therefore any line of held tip positions, judged from its own start. The finger's base is taken to be set back so that the tip meets the ball where that line starts; that moves the finger without turning it, so the needed direction and the contact normal are the same. Moving between the stroke line and the return line, at the two ends of the stroke, is a change of the held input and is not checked.
